pl-l4d19c3-d1e115.summary: Notes that the view that grace is transmitted even through a bad priest's ministry seems opposed by the Lord's threat to bad priests, 'I will curse your blessings', and 'woe to those who give life to souls that do not live and kill souls that do not die'. If the Lord curses their blessings and the souls they vivify do not live, how is the grace of blessing transmitted through them?

pl-l4d19c3-d1e124.summary: Reports that some refer 'I will curse your blessings' to heretics cut off from the Church and to the excommunicated, whose blessings become curses for those who follow their errors.
claims: Malachi's curse is applied to heretics and the excommunicated.

pl-l4d19c3-d1e130.summary: Reports that they apply 'they give life' to all priests who presume to bind or loose without the key of knowledge and the form of good life. No one should use the priest's office unless free of what he judges in others; otherwise he condemns himself.
claims: Binding and loosing without knowledge and good life is condemned.
The judge should be free of what he judges in others.

pl-l4d19c3-d1e137.summary: A heading encoded as a paragraph: 'What the ecclesiastical judge ought to be like'.

pl-l4d19c3-d1e140.summary: Quotes Augustine on what the judge of others must be: the priest to whom every sinner is brought should not be judged guilty of what he is ready to judge in another, for judging another he condemns himself. Let him know himself and purge in himself what he sees others bring; let him remember that the one without sin should cast the first stone, as Christ freed the sinful woman since no one could justly throw; the crime of priests who do not first judge themselves and then bind others is most detestable.
claims: The judge must first judge and purge himself.
Judging others while guilty is self-condemnation.

pl-l4d19c3-d1e155.summary: Continues Augustine: let the spiritual judge, as he is free of crime, not lack knowledge, so that he can discern what he judges. Let him question the sinner wisely about what he may not know or hide from shame, investigate the circumstances, place, and time, be kind, ready to raise him and share the burden, sweet in affection and discerning in variety, teaching perseverance. Let him beware of falling, lest he justly lose his judicial power; penance can regain grace but not at once restore the first power; Peter was restored, and fallen priests often were, but not as a right; where many fall and claim restoration as license, that hope must be cut off; elsewhere they may be restored.
claims: The judge must have knowledge to discern.
He must question wisely and investigate circumstances.
A fallen priest may lose his power; restoration is not a right.

pl-l4d19c3-d1e161.summary: Concludes that the priest who binds and looses must be discerning and just; otherwise he often kills souls that do not die and gives life to those that do not live, and falls under the judgment of the curse.
claims: The priest must be discerning and just.

pl-l4d19c3-d1e164.summary: Interprets Malachi's 'I will curse your blessings', whether of heretics and the excommunicated or of all priests lacking life and knowledge who presume to bless: I will curse what you possess by my blessings, making them turn to curse for you, since they bless the saints insincerely; or whatever you bless I will curse, since they bless evildoers and flatter rich sinners.
claims: God turns unworthy priests' blessings into curses for them.

pl-l4d19c3.summary: Faces texts that seem to deny that grace flows through bad priests: 'I will curse your blessings' and 'woe to those who give life to souls that do not live'. Some apply the first to heretics and the excommunicated, the second to priests who bind and loose without the key of knowledge and good life; no one should use the priestly office unless free of what he judges in others. Under the heading 'Qualis esse debeat iudex ecclesiasticus', Augustine describes the judge: he must not be guilty of what he judges, must have knowledge to discern, question wisely, investigate the circumstances, be kind and ready to share the burden, and avoid falling, lest he lose his power; restoration of fallen priests is allowed in some cases and denied in others. So the priest who binds and looses must be discerning and just; Malachi's curse means God turns their blessings into curses, or curses what they bless.
claims: Malachi's curse is applied to heretics, the excommunicated, or priests without knowledge and good life.
No one should judge others for what he himself is guilty of.
The ecclesiastical judge must be sinless in grave matters and have knowledge.
The confessor must investigate circumstances and be kind.
Fallen priests may or may not be restored, depending on circumstances.
The priest who binds and looses must be discerning and just.
